summary.title: Writing a C Compiler, Part 3: Binary Operators
summary.one_liner: You learn how to add binary arithmetic operators to a C compiler, handling operator precedence and left-associativity in a recursive descent parser and emitting x86 assembly for them using the stack.
keywords: how to handle minus as subtraction or negation
takeaways: Binary operators need a grammar that encodes precedence, typically with separate exp and term/factor levels.
Left recursion cannot be handled by a recursive descent parser, so use EBNF repetition ({ }) and build left-associative BinOp nodes in a loop.
Code generation for a binary op evaluates the first operand, pushes it on the stack, evaluates the second, then pops and combines.
Subtraction operand order matters with subl, and division requires moving the dividend into EAX and sign-extending with cdq before idivl.
summary.summary: This is part 3 of a series on writing a C compiler, where the author adds addition, subtraction, multiplication and division. It covers lexing (reusing the minus token), extending the AST with a BinOp node, and rewriting the grammar to fix precedence, associativity and left recursion using <term> and <factor> levels plus repetition. It includes pseudocode for parse_expression and parse_factor, then shows x86 code generation using push/pop on the stack, imul, subl, and idivl with cdq. It also gives GDB tips and further reading on precedence climbing and Pratt parsing.
